intent: The inventor is not the champion: a CHINA plate erased over the map, a dinner-table origin with books and a cigar-box lid, a THEN / NOW split from parlour game to 1988 Olympic sport, and three gold-medal bars that hand the story back to China.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country INVENTED table tennis?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: England. In the 1880s Victorians played it after dinner, with books for a net and a cigar-box lid for a bat.

lines.direction: tighten on southern England; the CHINA plate waits at the bottom and wipes away on 'China'; a scroll sticker on 'rules'; the London pin and tag on 'London' as the UK pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: Not China. The first rules and the first ping-pong sets were sold in London around 1901.

lines.direction: ease back over Britain; the PARLOUR GAME / OLYMPIC SPORT split lands on 'parlour'; a medal sticker on 'Olympic'; a trophy sticker on 'championships' as the UK pulses
lines.text: A parlour game became an Olympic sport in 1988. World championships began in London in 1926.

lines.direction: ease back further; three gold bars rise on 'China' with China towering; the Chinese flag-ball grins on 'golds'; a Japanese flag sticker on 'Japan'; a no-entry sticker and the English flag-ball, thinking, on 'none' as the UK pulses
lines.text: Since then China has won 37 of 42 Olympic golds. Japan, 1. The inventors, none.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Invented at dinner, mastered in China. Follow us.
